narrative: Material PL3__M51FD567 exhibits smooth, high-frequency demand averaging 1,190 units/day with a statistically significant declining trend (-1.62 units/day). Lead times are short but highly variable (CV=0.800), making lead-time variability the dominant buffer driver at 64.7% of total variance. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with SS=2,196, ROP=3,539, and Q=8,182 achieves 95% service level while reducing total annual inventory costs by 68.9% through fewer, larger replenishment orders. The storage capacity constraint bound the order quantity at 8,182 (down from unconstrained EOQ of 8,820).

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, near-continuous daily demand with short but unstable lead times is optimally served by a continuous-review (r,Q) system. The fixed order quantity aligns with the MOQ constraint (1,153) and allows EOQ optimisation, while the reorder point directly encodes lead-time demand variability into the trigger level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds at Q=8,182. Any upward revision to safety stock (e.g., adopting robust SS=2,761) would require a proportional reduction in order quantity to maintain the storage feasibility constraint, increasing ordering frequency and cost.
